bottomLine.interpretation: Conditional on Project Open Hand causing the modeled reduction in heart-failure hospitalizations, and counting only the short-term health-related quality-of-life loss of an acute admission, the best estimate is approximately $132.8 million per 10 QALYs (one better life). The positive-effect sensitivity is approximately $32.3 million-$7.8 billion. Because the intervention's randomized primary outcome was null and the favorable heart-failure result was exploratory, a null effect remains plausible and the true upper bound is not finite.

inputs.label: Conditional cost per heart-failure hospitalization averted
inputs.basis: Imported from the Project Open Hand native-outcome model. The range is conditional on a positive effect and combines course-cost and causal-effect sensitivities.

inputs.label: Short-term QALYs per heart-failure hospitalization averted
inputs.basis: Best: NICE modeled a 6-week utility dip from a worsening-heart-failure admission as a 0.064 decrement over a 3-month cycle, equal to 0.016 QALY. Low: acute-stay-only floor using ASCEND-HF's 0.11 gap between 24-hour inpatient and discharge utility over a six-day median stay (0.11 x 6 / 365 = 0.0018 QALY). High: McMurray et al.'s reported decrements of 0.105 in days 0-30 and 0.054 in days 31-90, integrated over 90 days (0.0175 QALY).

inputs.label: QALYs per one better life
inputs.basis: Market for Impact's shared comparison denominator. It is a reporting convention, not a clinical threshold or a claim that ten QALYs accrue to one identifiable person.

formula.bestCalculation: $212,500 / 0.016 QALY x 10 QALYs = $132,812,500 per better life
formula.rangeMethod: Optimistic positive-effect case divides the native model's $56,604 low cost by 0.0175 QALY and multiplies by 10. Pessimistic positive-effect case divides $1.4 million by 0.0018 QALY and multiplies by 10. A null causal effect is outside the numeric range and has no finite cost per QALY.

scope.population: Adults recently discharged after hospitalization with known heart failure; utility evidence is transferred from other acute and chronic heart-failure populations.
scope.duration: Short-term acute and post-discharge health-related quality-of-life loss through 90 days.
scope.personAllocation: One avoided hospitalization is assigned to one patient. No household multiplier is used.
scope.counterfactual: Usual post-discharge care without the modeled meal course, consistent with the native randomized comparison.
scope.overlapControls: Counts only short-term morbidity from the avoided admission. Excludes mortality, future readmissions, caregiver effects, food security, depression, adherence, medical cost savings, and any quality-of-life benefit of meals apart from avoiding the modeled admission.
scope.transferBoundary: The QALY weights are not Project Open Hand measurements. They come from international heart-failure trials and NICE modeling and may not match the San Francisco population, admission severity, length of stay, or recovery trajectory.

nullEffectBoundary: This bridge does not repair the causal uncertainty in the native model. The randomized primary all-cause hospitalization endpoint did not improve; the favorable heart-failure subgroup result was exploratory and provider-pooled. If Project Open Hand's true additional effect is zero, cost per 10 QALYs has no finite upper bound.
